observations: body L1-L2: the month is spelt «thōt» in L1 and «thōth» in L2.

body L2-L3: the vague year of Nabonassar that begins on 15 January 882 is the 1630th of the era, not «1631» (see the observation on the era on p. 209); the dates 15 January and 19 September 882 are right, and 8 pachōn is the 248th day of the year.
body L4-L6: at the equinox the Sun rises at 6h, so 4 3/4 hours before sunrise is 1h 15m after midnight; counted from the preceding noon, as astronomers count, that is 13h 15m.
body L7: the d of «ad» is printed broken.
body L6, L11-L12, L14-L16, L22-L23, L27, L29, L33, L36-L37: the dashes of «al–Battānī», «Al–Battānī» and «ar–Raqqah» are long dashes (5.3 to 5.5 pt).
body L17-L21, L29, L37: the minus signs are printed as long dashes (8.9 to 10.4 pt) and transcribed as minus signs; the dashes of «(882–139)» and «(25–18)» are the long dashes of the text (5.5 pt).

body L15-L22: 19h 40m − 13h 15m = 6h 25m; 743 Julian years less 7 days and 6h 25m are 742 Julian years + 358 days − 6h 25m; with the 186 leap days of the years 140 to 880 they make 742 vague years + 544 days − 6h 25m = 743 vague years + 179 days − 6h 25m = 743 vague years + 178 days + 17h 35m. Al-Battānī's interval, 17h 36m in L12, differs by one minute.

body L24-L26: Schram's time agrees with the equinox computed by modern theory, 18 September 882, about 23h 50m Terrestrial Time (11h 50m counted from noon); in universal time, about 38 minutes earlier, it is about 11h 12m, some 33 minutes after the time of al-Battānī's observation.
body L28-L30: 39° 3′ 57″ is 2h 36m 16s in time; 13h 15m − 2h 36m = 10h 39m and 11h 49m − 10h 39m = 1h 10m.
body L31, L38: heavy brackets open and close Schiaparelli's addition; the dash before his name measures 9.7 pt.
body L39: in the head the dash after «d)» measures 10.0 pt and is transcribed as a dash; that of «9–21» measures 5.4 pt, a long dash.
body L42: the full stop after «dividere» stands at the middle of the line.
